validity.note: An initially drafted URL label was rejected by Java and corrected before the final matrix. The preserved URL input and SVG are valid; no invalid input is counted.

java.finding: Java tries Sequence, Class, Activity, then Description factories and accepts the first factory that consumes the complete source.
Factory viability is command-driven. Multiline commands are recognized and consumed as complete blocks before their body lines can be considered as top-level commands.
Class registers its class, package, shared-symbol, link, title, and common command grammars, but not Description's bracket element grammar.
Description registers CommandLinkElement, shared symbol containers, CommandCreateElementFull, and multiline element commands in one command model.
The Description declaration grammar supports both `[Display] as Code` and `Code as [Display]`, preserving code and display separately.
The Description link grammar supports abbreviated direction tokens and bracketed line-style clauses in addition to full direction words.

rust.finding: Rust scans every raw line and suppresses bracket recognition only inside one hand-maintained class-leaf brace context. It does not model title, header, footer, legend, note, or other multiline command ownership.
Rust duplicates a reduced Description grammar. Its direction regex accepts only down/up/left/right, and its arrow regex excludes Java's bracketed style grammar.

The component parser can construct both alias directions when reached, but subtype scoring and command recognition do not consistently route reverse aliases or the broader Java link grammar to that parser.
No golden reads, fixture labels, SVG surgery, coordinate keys, or parity-affecting numeric constants were added. The defect is conceptual over-specialization, not mechanical fixture lookup.

findings: Rejected: the implementation models one special multiline context, class leaf bodies, instead of Java's general command-consumption model. Bracket-shaped title prose can still reject the Class candidate and eventually change the selected subtype.

Rejected: the duplicated Description link recognizer is narrower than Java CommandLinkElement. Links-only abbreviated directions and styled arrows leave the Class candidate viable and select CLASS with missing endpoints.

Rejected: the planned reverse-alias invariant is not established in shared containers. Reverse aliases are dropped or recreated as top-level code labels, losing display text, scope, source order, and links.

No fixture-keyed logic, golden dependency, SVG surgery, unexplained layout constant, or high-precision tuning was found. The implementation is nevertheless over-specialized to enumerated syntax rather than the underlying factory/command model.

The held-out matrix contains 19 Java-valid inputs across container, scope, alias direction, topology, order, direction, style, multiline-body, metadata, guard, URL, and class-control axes. Five are strict matches; eight failures directly contradict the claimed mechanism.
verdict_scope: The change recovers the targeted bare bracket cases and several held-outs, but it does not reproduce Java factory viability or the full Description bracket command model. General multiline command ownership, reverse aliases in shared containers, abbreviated directions, and styled links remain counterexamples.
